items.note: Story 1: farmers organize a cooperative creamery association at Larrow Green in 1889; main creamery built 1891. Gideon Vose as first president appears only in Section B (no credit travels), but the item has no REQUIRED line and its core fact is present.
Article VII quoted in substance: pay by pounds of butterfat found by test, not weight; the test of the station where he delivers governs.
Nowhere in Section A does the run state that this rule is what made a wrong test cost money (payment by weight would have cost nobody anything).
Effie Loomis never appears anywhere; Teague and Sill appear only in D/F, and no officer roles are given in Section A.
Story 5 dates Selby Vose's management from 1911 (planted error); 'Gideon's son' appears only in Section B.
The station-gain ledger line is described only in B3 and C3, never inside Section A.
Story 1: skimming station seven miles up the valley, built winter 1895-96, opened 4 May 1896, glassware borrowed from Larrow Green.

No description of the working system (weighing at intake, composite sample per patron, cream to Larrow Green / skim returned). Only the graduated-neck point surfaces, embedded in the defect explanation.
Ammon & Sons of Tarnet, invoice of 14 April 1897, outfit in use from 1 May 1897.
Full invoice recited: 6 doz pipettes marked 17.6 c.c., 12 doz bottles, acid measure, hand tester, freight, $77.93.
Story 2: 0.19 'precise and unvarying ... in every month of the year, in the flush of June and the depth of February alike.'
The 'cannot be checked without a burette, and there was none in the county' point is made only in Section F, not in Section A.
Keddie tester from the 4 May 1896 opening, twenty-nine seasons, dismissed 30 April 1925.
Test book named but no bench routine, no columns (date/patron/pounds/test/fat), no crossed-and-initialed corrections.
The summary leaf is never reproduced; no 1896 average of 3.80 on borrowed glass against 3.61 from 1898 anywhere in Section A.
Story 4: broke 8 May 1911, borrowed measure to 10 July, tests at 3.80, back to 3.61 on the return, question mark in the book.
Orra his wife, Emmet her brother (Story 5), Emmet the largest patron (Story 1).
1919 circular over the manager's signature (Story 5); Keddie's 17 March 1925 statement that he could not explain the figures and never took cream (Story 7).
Died 1934 'with the imputation on him' - the bolded element.
Six farms on Hessel Bottom, largest Emmet Brant's.
Weigh book begun 1 January 1897; his scale beside the station's, daily, noted 'agreeing' - the two scales agreed.

1902 complaints of record given. The run gives Larrow Green as '3.78-3.80' (a range leading with the correct 3.78) and states the 0.19 as separation 'from the truth', so it does not commit the keyed 0.19 Hollow-vs-Green conflation.
Grigg's committee named but the run says it 'sampled the herds of Hessel Bottom every month throughout 1908' - the planted whole-of-1908 error; Jan-Mar required.
Brant's 1910 year (200,000 lb at 3.42) appears only in Section C; no proportional-loss point anywhere.
'Roy Brant later kept the same book' only; no 1929 passage and no 1958 lending to Ivy in Section A.
Redlow Ridge and Alder Corners named, but Vessey County is absent and Jerome Cudd is never named as founder; the key gates on company, ridge, county and Cudd.
Four of the six Hessel Bottom farms hauled over the ridge in summer, 1915-1930.
REQUIRED two of four independence elements. Section A names the artifact only; no other county, bench, glassware or uncompared book. 'Independent testing' appears in Section C, not A.
Same four men's milk at 3.78-3.82 (avg 3.80) at Alder Corners against Hollow's 3.61, over sixteen summers 1915-1930.
Story 2 states the same milk tested elsewhere proved the milk sound and the Ostrey Hollow tests systematically wrong.
Rosalie Cudd appears only in a citation line; no daughter relation, no 1941-1962, no copying sixteen seasons for Ivy.
Strawn named and his disinterest stated, but the circuit is dated 'from 1908 onward' (planted error) and 1936 is absent.
Lactometer for added water at every visit and never once found any - the bolded element.
12 June 1923, pipettes run against a calibrated burette, whole lot condemned.
'he wrote nothing about what they might have been doing for the twenty-six years prior ... The inspector did not infer backward.'
Order 28 June and reply 2 July are right, but the run gives the post-1923 average as 3.85, not 3.80 - the key's stated loss condition.
Crate placed in the loft over the intake room under a tarpaulin in 1923 - the aspect the key assigns this item.
January 1925 petition; the date carries the item.
Frick chairman, three sittings 17 March - 4 May 1925, two of them in the station weigh room.
Three explanations argued and none accepted: watering (Vose), tester theft, wet hay.
Four books listed including Strawn's 1923 notebook, with Frick's reflection that the answer may have been in the room.
Dismissed 30 April 1925 without a finding; award 4 May 1925 of $3,800 'without admission' charged to the station account.
Says only 'less than a fifth of the patrons' own reckoning' (a corrupted $19,600/67,000 lb reckoning); no identity between the award's account and the station-gain account since 1898.
Ivy Keddie, granddaughter (with the great-niece error corrected), graduate student at the State Agricultural College at Farland; Vaught named as co-author.
No account of assembling the five record series that had never been in one room.
February 1958 and the station loft are right, but the run says eleven pipettes survived; nine is required.
9 March 1958 and the burette are right, but the mean delivery is given as 16.27 c.c., short 1.33 c.c. / 7.56 percent.

Section A's account of the measurement asserts 92.44 percent and a true average of 3.905, contradicting the required 95-percent-of-true chain; the '5% low readings' clause sits incoherently beside it.
REQUIRED all four. 40,000,000 lb and 76,000 lb appear, but the money in Section A is $19,600 (not $19,000) and the ledger identity is absent.
Bulletin 471, October 1958, clears him; 33 years after dismissal, 24 after death (35-after-condemnation missing but the core fact is present).
Granddaughter.
Derivation given: Ansel > Duncan (b. 1894) > Ivy (b. 1931), on Duncan's family record.
Second cousins with the full derivation through Emmet/Orra as siblings and Roy/Duncan as first cousins.
Abstention item A08 not addressed: the run says 'brother and sister' and never raises full-vs-half or its irrelevance to the answer. No definite assertion either way, so no gullibility deduction.
Gideon Vose, his father, first president and author of the by-laws.
Significance stated: Article VII made the station's test decide pay with no appeal, so Selby was enforcing his father's rule against the consequences of a fault in the instrument it made decisive.
Abstention item A01 asserted: headline verdict 'There was no direct blood relationship between the Vose family and the Keddie family,' closing 'No evidence supports a blood relationship.'
Lost with the assertion; the run treats a family member's denial as settling the record rather than as one uncorroborated statement.
Gives 16.27 / 17.6 = 0.9244, short 7.56 percent. Required: 0.95, short 5 percent.
Explicitly resolves to true 3.80, recorded 3.61, short 0.19 (declining Vaught's 3.905).
$19,000; $3,800 received = 20 percent, one fifth. Both money and fraction given.
Uses the station-wide 3.80 instead of 3.42/0.95 = 3.60; gets 760 lb rather than 360 lb.
$190 rather than $86.40 (and no statement of using a period-average price with correct working).
1,444,000 lb credited.
1,520,000 lb given as the answer.
Both denominators named explicitly: 5.26 percent of fat credited to patrons, 5.0 percent of fat actually received. Avoids the NT-20 trap ('of the true fat').
$77.93, with the five line items added.
72 pipettes correct, but the shortfall is given as 1.33 c.c.; both elements required.

'26 years, 1 month, 12 days' - not the keyed 26 years 6 weeks / 26 years 1 month 11 days / 26 years 42 days, and this section is exact-match. Full years also given as 'roughly 1898-1923' rather than 1898-1922.
Abstention item A02 asserted: first season stated as 1,100,000 lb on Kyle's memory (also asserted as ~1.1 million in Story 1).
Variable named: the measuring glass / pipette, the one object that changed.
Constants listed: tester, method, machinery, herds and farms, season, acid, bottles.
3.61 to 3.80 across the nine weeks, back to 3.61 on 10 July.

Both halves: cause in the glassware and not in adulteration, theft, biology or pasture; and limits stated (does not fix the precise defect, does not prove it ran from 1897, does not settle deliberateness).
Three valid distinct reasons attributed to three narrators: the 1911 interval (r11/r22), Sill's heavy cream in the receiving book (r14/r23), the Alder Corners record (r10).
Independence argued explicitly ('no single narrator supports more than one') and the 1911 interval named as holding without the 1958 measurement.
Abstention item A09 asserted: 'Did the bookkeeper question the ledger entries? No.' A headline verdict.
Answers the literal question yes - he knew the station's tests ran low - citing the 1919 circular.

REQUIRED three of five: signed the annual ledger sheets carrying the station-gain line; wrote the 1919 circular; promoted the watering theory used at the 1925 arbitration (B3). 'Manager from 1913' fails (run says 1911).

Abstention item A03 not declined and asserted: 'Vose knew tests ran low (evidenced by the 1919 warning and his observation of the consistent station gain)' and 'Vose knew something was systematically wrong with Hollow tests' - the key's own discriminator for an A03 assertion (the station-gain line telling him so / the tests being wrong).

Capped. Four qualifying resolutions with method: $3,500 vs $3,800 (corroboration plus documentary access), Kyle's 'twenty-two' vs 12 June 1923 (document over memory), great-niece vs granddaughter (family record and the source's own correction), $77.39 vs $77.93 (arithmetic on the reproduced invoice). None credited at E-b, per the key's never-both rule.

No near-tie pair correctly identified. The run raises the idea and retracts it ('only Cleve states $3,500 ... This is not a two narrators case'), and on $77.39 it names the Chronicle and Falke as the pair rather than the Chronicle and Ammon herself.

A04 asserted rather than declined ('The defect arose from a mold failure in manufacture'); A06 gets only a parenthetical 'source unspecified' with no statement of what the sources do establish; A10 never raised.
The run states the opposite: 'No narrator contradicts itself on the page within these retellings.'

Cause named but sized wrong: 16.27 c.c., 92.44 percent, 7.56 percent short, with 0.19 asserted as its consequence (it is not); the cessation is given as a 1924 average of 3.85; the 1896 borrowed-glass season is not used for the onset.
Watering named (Vose, 1919 circular) and defeated with Strawn's lactometer, the Alder Corners cheese record, and the 1911 interval.
Theft named and defeated with the specific point that a theft makes cream arrive light and it arrived heavy every year in Sill's book, plus the 1911 interval.

Bog hay named (1908 committee) and defeated with the year-round flatness, the Alder Corners book and the 1923 glass change without land change. Bulletin 214's finding is misquoted as 'two tenths' - deducted separately, but the defeat is specific.
Abstention item A07 asserted: 'Did the 1925 board ever examine the condemned glassware? No.' plus 'The glassware crate was not presented.'

Abstention item A05 not declined: presents only Duncan's pole (never Frick's contrary recollection) and asserts in its own voice 'His suspicion in 1911 was never pursued, never tested, never vindicated.'
169 words by count, not the claimed 149; cap is 150.
Names no record series except the 1958 measurement; 'contemporaneous records' is not a named series. Five required.
Carries 16.27 c.c. as a headline number.
REQUIRED four of six covering both ends: from 1897, 76,000 lb / $19,000, condemned 1923, explained 1958. (Ansel not named; 'one part in twenty' not given.)

deductions.reason: Corruption: Selby Vose manager 'since 1911' asserted (Story 5, B3, D3)
Corruption: Strawn's circuit / lactometer visits dated 'from 1908 onward' (Story 5, F2)
Corruption: 1908 committee 'sampled the herds of Hessel Bottom every month throughout 1908' (Story 3)
Corruption: Bulletin 214 said to find 'two tenths' depression in winter (Story 3, F4)
Corruption: post-condemnation station average asserted as 3.85 in 1924 (Story 6, F1), and 'actually 3.85' as the true Hollow figure (Story 3)
Corruption: eleven pipettes said to have survived in the crate (Story 8, C1, F1)
Corruption: mean pipette delivery asserted as 16.27 c.c. throughout (Stories 4 and 8, C1a, C4b, F1, G)
Corruption: 67,000 lb of butterfat asserted as a real loss figure (Story 7, and endorsed in E6 as a genuine alternative measure)
Gullibility: abstention item A01 (Vose-Keddie kinship) answered with a flat denial in B4
Gullibility: abstention item A02 (1896 first-season intake) answered as 1,100,000 lb in C5b and Story 1
Gullibility: abstention item A03 (did the manager know the tests understated the fat) asserted in D3 via the station-gain line and 'something was systematically wrong with Hollow tests'
Gullibility: abstention item A04 (accident or substitution) asserted in F1 as 'a mold failure in manufacture'
Gullibility: abstention item A05 (what the tester believed) asserted in F6 as a suspicion of the glass, on Duncan's pole alone
Gullibility: abstention item A07 (did the board examine the glassware) answered 'No' in F5
Gullibility: abstention item A09 (did the bookkeeper ever question the entries) answered 'No' in D2
